searchText: Is the networking and consensus for DVT well specified enough so that different implementations can be used in the same validator (for example a distributed node with half running obol and the other half running ssv)? <@550420431744794624> <@555483069038198827> ^ Right now the two implementations are not compatible with one another but at some point both hope to have multiple independent interoperable clients Is there a reason why the two haven't come together to standardize? Increased interop between them (and others) seems like a good goal We at obol went the route of implementing Obol as a distributed validator middleware that allows the existing validator clients to operate together as a distributed validator. The specs right now entail creating a standalone validator client. You can read more about our approach here https://ethresear.ch/t/distributed-validator-middlewares-and-the-aggregation-duty/13044 There is an emerging EF spec but it’s far from complete. SSV has a pretty complete spec detailed here https://github.com/bloxapp/ssv-spec Current EF spec uses a remote signer approach and doesn’t require any ethereum spec/ standard changes Interesting. Thanks for the info
